content_voiceover: This slide shows the same type of study but for apixaban, a direct factor Xa inhibitor, from the Journal of Thrombosis and Haemostasis 2014. On the left, aPTT rises only modestly with increasing apixaban concentration and stays largely within or close to the normal range, shown by the orange band, even across the therapeutic zone. On the right, the INR panel shows a similarly shallow rise, staying close to one until concentrations climb well beyond typical therapeutic levels. Compare this with the dabigatran slide we just saw. Unlike dabigatran, which produces a clear dose dependent rise in aPTT, apixaban has a much more blunted effect on both aPTT and PT and INR. This is a critical board concept, a normal aPTT or normal PT or INR does not exclude clinically relevant apixaban, or by extension other factor Xa inhibitors like rivaroxaban. Routine coagulation screens simply are not reliable for these drugs, which is why a drug specific chromogenic anti factor Xa assay is needed whenever quantification actually matters.
keypoints: Apixaban minimally prolongs aPTT and PT or INR even at therapeutic levels
Normal aPTT or PT does not exclude clinically relevant apixaban
Routine coagulation screens are unreliable for factor Xa inhibitors
Drug calibrated chromogenic anti-Xa assay is needed for quantification
